_readme: Courtesies the desk should answer like a person rather than search for.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the built-in list started at twenty items and the
desk's own courtesy table is longer. Reporting the gap one string at a
time — 'Good day', 'Bravo', 'Safe travels' — is nobody's good use of an
afternoon. Put the rest of the table here instead, without a deploy.
'phrases' maps a whole message to a category. Use it when the words only
mean the courtesy together: 'good day' is a greeting, but 'good' and
'day' apart are not. Case, spacing and trailing punctuation are ignored.
'words' adds a single word to a category's core vocabulary. Use it for a
word that carries the courtesy on its own, like 'bravo'. A message
matches a category when every content word is known to it and at least
one is core, so a stray word still sends the message to a real answer.
CATEGORIES: greeting, thanks, apology, attention, farewell, praise,
well_wish, meeting, affirm, decline. An entry naming anything else is
ignored, so a typo cannot take the desk down.
WHAT NOT TO PUT HERE: anything a member might mean literally. This layer
answers without searching the knowledge base, so a phrase added here can
never reach a real answer. 'Help me' is a request, not a courtesy.
A courtesy is only matched when it is essentially the whole message, so
'Good day, when does the branch open?' still answers the branch question.
